items.title: Carelon adds coverage for Guardant's Shield colorectal blood test, taking covered lives to ~90 million
items.summary: Carelon Healthcare Services, which manages specialty benefits for Blue Cross Blue Shield plans across 26 states, updated its clinical guidelines to cover Guardant Health's Shield blood-based colorectal cancer screening test, effective 15 November. Guardant says the policy lifts total covered lives for Shield to approximately 90 million, or roughly 75% of the eligible US population. Shield is FDA-approved for primary CRC screening in average-risk adults aged 45+. (Figures are company-reported and approximate.)
items.why: The single clearest signal yet that blood-based cancer screening is crossing from cash-pay novelty into reimbursed standard of care — the same transition that will eventually reset consumer price expectations for SPOT-MAS and other MCED offers in Singapore.

items.title: Oura files S-1 for a Nasdaq IPO as it pushes deeper into preventive health
items.summary: Smart ring maker Oura filed its registration statement with the SEC for a proposed IPO, planning to trade under the ticker "OURA". MobiHealthNews frames the filing around the company's continued expansion into preventive health. Reported financials circulating alongside the filing (revenue and paid-member counts) should be read directly from the S-1 rather than secondary coverage.
items.why: A consumer wearable listing on a preventive-health story sets a public-market benchmark for the continuous-monitoring layer that sits upstream of Protocol's biomarker panels — and a likely future competitor for the same annual wallet.

items.title: STAREE: atorvastatin cuts major cardiovascular events 30% in healthy over-70s, but not disability-free survival
items.summary: In a 9,971-participant, double-blind Australian primary-prevention trial presented in a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026 and published simultaneously in the New England Journal of Medicine, atorvastatin 40 mg daily reduced major cardiovascular events versus placebo over a median 5.9 years (6.0% vs 8.3%; HR 0.70). Disability-free survival did not differ significantly (12.8% vs 13.6%; HR 0.94, p=0.25). Muscle, liver and diabetes-related adverse events were more frequent on atorvastatin.
items.why: The first randomised evidence that statin primary prevention works in people over 70 — a direct, guideline-grade justification for lipid panels and pharmacological intervention in Protocol's older screening cohort, while the null healthspan endpoint tempers the longevity pitch.

items.title: ESC Congress 2026 closes as largest ever, with AI as the spotlight theme
items.summary: The European Society of Cardiology reported that 33,800 healthcare professionals from 170 countries attended ESC Congress 2026 in Munich (28–31 August), its largest flagship meeting to date. The programme included 12 Hot Line sessions and 30 Late-Breaking Science sessions, three new Clinical Practice Guidelines, and the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction. More than 180 studies were published simultaneously in leading journals.
items.why: Cardiovascular medicine's biggest stage spent the week on AI-assisted risk detection and prevention guidelines — the evidence base Protocol's cardiometabolic screening claims will be measured against over the next 12 months.

items.title: Scan.com raises $220M to expand US medical imaging access
items.summary: Scan.com secured $220 million in financing to expand its US medical imaging business, comprising a $90 million Series C equity round and $130 million in debt facilities, according to MobiHealthNews.
items.why: Capital keeps flowing to consumer-routed diagnostic access rather than to new assays — a reminder that distribution and booking friction, not test menus, is where the preventive-health category is currently competing.

items.title: Elucid raises $55M for AI cardiovascular imaging software
items.summary: Elucid closed a $55 million round to expand its platforms and advance its BioIntegrated FFR-CT technology through the FDA clearance process, MobiHealthNews reported.
items.why: Plaque-level imaging analytics are moving toward regulatory clearance, which would let clinics quantify cardiovascular risk beyond lipids — a plausible future add-on SKU above Protocol's 100+ biomarker panel.

items.title: South Korean retinal AI screens for dementia and predicts future risk
items.summary: An explainable AI model developed in South Korea screens for dementia and predicts future risk from retinal images, outperforming the conventional CAIDE Dementia Risk Score in both detection and prediction, according to MobiHealthNews Asia. Performance figures should be confirmed against the underlying publication before being quoted.
items.why: Retinal imaging is cheap, fast and already routine in Asia — making it a credible near-term cognitive-risk module for an Asian screening clinic, and a category Protocol's Singapore competitors could bolt on quickly.

items.title: GE HealthCare secures CE mark for photon-counting CT system
items.summary: GE HealthCare received CE mark certification for its Photonova Spectra photon-counting CT system, putting it into direct competition with Siemens Healthineers in a technology designed to deliver clearer images than conventional CT, MedTech Dive reported.
items.why: Photon-counting CT lowers dose while raising resolution, which strengthens the case for imaging as a routine component of premium executive screening rather than a specialist referral.

items.title: Vitality acquires digital health engagement company Icario
items.summary: Vitality, the behaviour-linked insurance and wellness group, acquired Icario, a digital health engagement company, MobiHealthNews reported. Deal terms were not detailed in the coverage reviewed.
items.why: An insurer-adjacent player buying engagement infrastructure signals that adherence and behaviour change, not the screening event, is where margin is being defended — the same logic behind Protocol's screening-plus-coaching model.
